findings.text: blocking: _NEO4J_STORE_BASE is the literal string "$HOME/.local/share/iter-codex/neo4j" and reaches the scan as env SERVICE_STORE='$HOME/...' with no shell expansion, so the case pattern at :666 compares a real cwd against the literal and never matches; reproduced with the landed scan script, a fake process whose cwd is .../neo4j/data yields zero HOLD lines at the production default and one HOLD line with the expanded path. Every default-store caller is therefore inert: stop_local_store_holders (:857), _kill_neo4j_on_node (:1169), _wait_for_store_release (:838), and the holder guard at the top of _clean_neo4j_locks (:1151), so deploy_neo4j (:1333-1334) will dd/replace neostore* files while a live Neo4j holds the store — the hazard the goal's third requirement exists to prevent, replacing a pgrep guard that did detect the JVM.

blocking: _kill_embed_orphans signals nothing whenever _get_service_job(_EMBED_JOB) lists nothing, but all three production callers invoke it in exactly that state: services.py:1371 deploy_embed (which returns early when a job is RUNNING and whose comment says it clears orphans surviving scancel), services.py:1406 deploy_embed_noslurm (a nohup embed has no SLURM job at all), and iter_codex/cli/embed.py:684 after scancel. The embed orphan cleanup the goal's fifth requirement covers is dead, and the callers still print 'Cleaned up N worker process(es)' / 'Killed rogue embed process(es)', so a second embed server can start on the same port with no signal sent.

non-blocking: age is computed from stat -c %Y on the /proc/<pid> directory, whose mtime is the current time (measured: /proc/1 mtime equals now), so every listed process prints an age of 0s and the requirement to print each pid with its age is not met. iter_codex/cli/tunnel.py:808 already shows the correct idiom, ps -o uid=,etime=,args=.

non-blocking: _run_remote("scancel {job_id}", check=False) discards the scheduler cancel's output, so requirement 6 — the scheduler cancel and each signal print what they did — is unmet for this one command, though every signal does print.

non-blocking: _wait_for_store_release calls _select_processes(node) with no job_id, so on a compute node the containerised Neo4j that can still hold the store is attributable by neither the store path nor the job cgroup; after the default-store literal at :647 is repaired this gate can still report release while the holder exits.

item_aggregate: 5 of 5 checklist items read; both blocking findings are in production call paths the node rewrote.
